hook.text: Antarctic krill weigh just 2 grams each—but their total biomass exceeds that of all humans on Earth.

buildup.text: Euphausia superba swarm in dense schools—sometimes turning the ocean surface pink over square kilometers.

discovery.text: Krill eat ice algae and phytoplankton—then feed whales, seals, penguins, and fish. They're the hub of everything.

twist.text: Krill populations have declined 80% since the 1970s in some areas—as sea ice decreases, so does their food.

climax.text: Commercial krill fishing adds pressure—used for fish feed and omega-3 supplements, it's growing rapidly.

punchline.text: A tiny shrimp holds the entire Antarctic food web together.

quiz.question: Why are krill essential to Antarctic ecosystems?
options: They connect ice algae to whales, seals, and penguins
